title: PLHessianLipschitzKurtosis.lean

problem_class.label: nonconvex
problem_class.details: The objective may be nonconvex; global PL, gradient Lipschitz continuity, and Hessian Lipschitz continuity are imposed without convexity.

problem_class.label: pl
problem_class.details: Unconstrained minimization with an attained global minimum f*, global inequality 2μ(f(x)−f*) ≤ ‖∇f(x)‖², and initial gap f(x0)−f* ≤ Δ. Parameters satisfy 0 < μ ≤ L and Δ ≥ 0.

oracle.label: stochastic_gradient
oracle.details: Each query x returns g(x,ξ) using a fresh IID seed, with E[g(x,ξ)] = ∇f(x). Only gradient observations are supplied. All Params, including L, μ, ρ, σ, K, Δ, ε and x0, are public; f and the oracle distribution are hidden.

distinctive_assumptions.label: bounded_variance
distinctive_assumptions.details: Uniform centered second-moment bound E‖g(x,ξ)−∇f(x)‖² ≤ σ², with σ ≥ 0.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: The ambient space is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its Borel measurable structure.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: Globally L-Lipschitz gradient and differentiable gradient with globally ρ-Lipschitz Hessian in operator norm, ρ ≥ 0. Uniform centered fourth-moment bound E‖g(x,ξ)−∇f(x)‖⁴ ≤ Kσ⁴ with K ≥ 1; no exponential-tail or sample-gradient smoothness assumption.

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: Return a measurable point X with integrable objective gap and E[f(X)−f*] ≤ ε, where ε > 0. The allowed algorithm is restricted to WindowSgd.method with positive constant step size and natural-number window parameters.

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: Expectation is over algorithm randomization and IID oracle seeds. The extracted budget is a fixed cap on all stochastic-gradient oracle calls, rather than an expected stopping cost.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: This specializes stochastic PL optimization through the combination of global Hessian Lipschitz continuity, a quantitative centered fourth-moment bound, and a restricted constant-step window algorithm family.

descriptionHtml:
Window SGD under the PL Condition

We consider minimizing a possibly nonconvex function f:E→R on a finite-dimensional real inner product space E. The objective has a Lipschitz gradient, a Lipschitz Hessian, and a global minimizer x⋆, and satisfies the Polyak–Łojasiewicz condition. A given starting point has bounded objective gap. At x∈E, the oracle returns g(x,ξ), an unbiased gradient estimate using a fresh independent sample ξ, with uniformly bounded second and fourth noise moments. Window SGD must produce a measurable output x¯∈E with integrable objective gap and E[f(x¯)−f(x⋆)]≤ε, where ε>0 and expectation includes sampling and algorithm randomness.

The optimization problem is minx∈Ef(x). Write ∥⋅∥ for the inner product norm and ∥⋅∥op for the induced operator norm. Fix a starting point x0∈E, a measurable sample space Ω, and parameters 0<μ≤L,ρ,σ,Δ≥0,K≥1,ε>0. The algorithm receives E, Ω, L, μ, ρ, σ, K, Δ, ε, and x0.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Gradient and Hessian regularity). The function f is Fréchet differentiable on E, and its gradient is Fréchet differentiable on E. For every x,y∈E, ∥∇f(x)−∇f(y)∥≤L∥x−y∥,∥∇2f(x)−∇2f(y)∥op≤ρ∥x−y∥. Here ∇2f(x):E→E is the derivative of the gradient.

Assumption 2 (Polyak–Łojasiewicz condition and initial gap). There exists x⋆∈E such that, for every x∈E, f(x⋆)≤f(x),2μ(f(x)−f(x⋆))≤∥∇f(x)∥2, and the given starting point satisfies f(x0)−f(x⋆)≤Δ.

Assumption 3 (Independent stochastic gradients and fourth moments). There is a probability measure ν on Ω and a jointly measurable map g:E×Ω→E. The measurable samples (ξk)k≥0 are mutually independent, each with law ν. At its kth call, the oracle returns g(x,ξk) for any query x∈E. For every fixed x∈E, g(x,ξ) is Bochner integrable under ξ∼ν, and Eξ∼ν[g(x,ξ)]=∇f(x). Writing e(x,ξ)=g(x,ξ)−∇f(x), both ∥e(x,ξ)∥2 and ∥e(x,ξ)∥4 are integrable, with Eξ∼ν[∥e(x,ξ)∥2]≤σ2,Eξ∼ν[∥e(x,ξ)∥4]≤Kσ4.

Our formulation is algorithm-specific: we analyze Window SGD. The algorithm chooses a constant step size η>0 and integers Ta,Tb≥0 from its inputs. Independently of the oracle samples, it draws τ uniformly from {0,…,Tb} and sets H=Ta+τ. Starting from the given x0, its recurrence for a budget of N≥0 oracle calls is gk=g(xk,ξk),xk+1={xk−ηgk,k<H,xk,k≥H,k=0,…,N−1. The output is x¯=xN. Calls continue to count after the iterate is frozen. Thus, when N≥Ta+Tb, the output is the SGD iterate at the uniformly selected index H; a smaller budget truncates the updates at N.

Let P be the joint law of τ and the oracle samples. The output must be measurable, its objective gap must be integrable under P, and the accuracy requirement is EP[f(x¯)−f(x⋆)]≤ε.

comparisonHtml:
On a finite-dimensional real inner-product space, f has an attained minimum f⋆=f(x⋆), an L-Lipschitz gradient, and a differentiable gradient with ρ-Lipschitz Hessian. Globally, 2μ(f−f⋆)≤∥∇f∥2, with 0<μ≤L and f(x0)−f⋆≤Δ. The jointly measurable oracle uses IID samples of law p0: ∫g(x,ω)dp0=∇f(x) and, for e=g−∇f, ∫∥e∥2dp0≤σ2, ∫∥e∥4dp0≤Kσ4. Here ρ,σ,Δ≥0, K≥1. The setup requires constant-step SGD with a uniformly sampled final-window iterate x^; the target is ∫(f(x^)−f⋆)dP≤ε, ε>0, under its execution probability law P.

Stochastic optimization under PLHessianLipschitzKurtosis.
Result Oracle complexity Novelty Limitations
(1) KappaFreeSgdPLHessian (Ours) (⋆⋆⋆) (review) O([κ5/4+Kκ3/2σ2ρ2μ4+σ2με]ℓ)
(2) SGD (Khaled and Richtárik 2020, Thm. 3, Cor. 2) O(κ[1+log⁡(1+Δ/ε)]+κσ2με) (1): statistical factor κ→ℓ; total gain κ/ℓ when ℓ≪κ and ε≪ℓ−1min{σ2μ3/4L1/4,μ7/2KL1/2ρ2}. For μ=σ=ρ=Δ=1, K=3, ε=κ−2: O(κ3)→O(κ2log⁡κ). (1) adds Hessian regularity and kurtosis; κ5/4ℓ initialization and a ρ-term. Random window replaces last iterate. Noise term worsens when ℓ≫κ.
(3) Weighted SGD (Stich 2019, Thm. 5); strongly convex restriction O(κ[1+log⁡(1+κΔ/ε)]+σ2με) (1): scope extends from strong convexity to PL, allowing non-isolated minimizers. (1) on the strongly convex overlap: extra κ1/4 initialization factor, ρ-term and statistical logarithm; needs ρ,K.
(4) Ruppert–Polyak averaging (Gadat and Panloup 2017, Thm. 2); isolated-minimizer restriction Derived bound: O(1+trΣ⋆δ+(Cδ)4/5) for E∥x¯−x⋆∥2≤δ, steps γn−3/4. Requires coercivity, unique critical point, ∇2f(x⋆)≻0, Lipschitz noise covariance and L4 consistency. C is non-explicit. (1) allows non-isolated minimizers and gives explicit parameter dependence. Rates are not comparable: squared-distance accuracy and covariance/consistency assumptions differ.
(5) Lower bound (Masiha et al. 2026, Thm. 4.3, Rem. 4.6); broader smooth PL class Ω(κσ2με) for 0<ε≤Δ/10, σ>0; all randomized first-order methods with bounded-variance gradient access. (1) improves the statistical dependence on a narrower subclass. The hard instances lack Lipschitz Hessians; this is not an improvement on the full smooth PL class.

Abbr: κ=L/μ; ℓ=1+log⁡(1+κΔ/ε). Costs count individual stochastic-gradient calls, including the initial window burn-in. δ is squared-distance tolerance; x¯ is an averaged iterate; Σ⋆=[∇2f(x⋆)]−1S(x⋆)[∇2f(x⋆)]−1, with S the noise covariance; C is the remainder constant. L4 consistency means E∥xn−x⋆∥4=O(γn2); γ>0 is the stepsize scale.

import LongTails.Template
import Mathlib.Probability.Distributions.Uniform
import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Basic
import LongTails.Setups.StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Gradient.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Module.FiniteDimension

namespace OracleTemplate.WindowSgd

variable {E : Type} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]

noncomputable def method (η : ℝ) (Ta Tb : ℕ) (x0 : E) : Algorithm E E E where
  Seed := Fin (Tb + 1)
  law := ⟨(PMF.uniformOfFintype (Fin (Tb + 1))).toMeasure, inferInstance⟩
  State := ℕ × ℕ × E
  initial τ := (Ta + τ.val, 0, x0)
  query s := (0, s.2.2)
  update s g := if s.2.1 < s.1 then (s.1, s.2.1 + 1, s.2.2 - η • g) else s
  output s := s.2.2

end OracleTemplate.WindowSgd

open MeasureTheory

namespace LongTails.Setups.PLHessianLipschitzKurtosis

open OracleTemplate

structure Params where
  E : Type
  [normedE : NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [innerE : InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  [finiteE : FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
  [measurableE : MeasurableSpace E]
  [borelE : BorelSpace E]
  Ω : Type
  [measurableΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω]
  L : ℝ
  μ : ℝ
  ρ : ℝ
  σ : ℝ
  K : ℝ
  Δ : ℝ
  ε : ℝ
  x0 : E

attribute [instance] Params.normedE Params.innerE Params.finiteE Params.measurableE
  Params.borelE Params.measurableΩ

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Params
  Instance p := p.E → ℝ
  Query p := p.E
  Reply p := p.E
  Output p := p.E
  publicInput p := p
  valid p := 0 < p.μ ∧ p.μ ≤ p.L ∧ 0 ≤ p.ρ ∧ 0 ≤ p.σ ∧ 1 ≤ p.K ∧ 0 ≤ p.Δ ∧ 0 < p.ε
  admissible p f O :=
    ∃ (g : p.E → p.Ω → p.E) (P0 : ProbabilityMeasure p.Ω) (P : ProbabilityMeasure (ℕ → p.Ω)),
    LongTails.Setups.StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.IID
      (fun k (ξ : ℕ → p.Ω) => ξ k) (P0 : Measure _) (P : Measure _) ∧
    O = { Seed := fun _ => p.Ω
          law := P
          answer := fun _ (_, x) seed => g x seed } ∧
    (∀ x, HasGradientAt f (gradient f x) x) ∧
    (∀ x y, ‖gradient f x - gradient f y‖ ≤ p.L * ‖x - y‖) ∧
    Differentiable ℝ (gradient f) ∧
    (∀ x y, ‖fderiv ℝ (gradient f) x - fderiv ℝ (gradient f) y‖ ≤ p.ρ * ‖x - y‖) ∧
    (∃ xstar, IsMinOn f Set.univ xstar ∧
      (∀ x, 2 * p.μ * (f x - f xstar) ≤ ‖gradient f x‖ ^ 2) ∧ f p.x0 - f xstar ≤ p.Δ) ∧
    Measurable (Function.uncurry g) ∧
    (∀ x, Integrable (g x) (P0 : Measure _)) ∧
    (∀ x, ∫ ω, g x ω ∂(P0 : Measure _) = gradient f x) ∧
    (∀ x, Integrable (fun ω => ‖g x ω - gradient f x‖ ^ 2) (P0 : Measure _)) ∧
    (∀ x, Integrable (fun ω => ‖g x ω - gradient f x‖ ^ 4) (P0 : Measure _)) ∧
    (∀ x, ∫ ω, ‖g x ω - gradient f x‖ ^ 2 ∂(P0 : Measure _) ≤ p.σ ^ 2) ∧
    (∀ x, ∫ ω, ‖g x ω - gradient f x‖ ^ 4 ∂(P0 : Measure _) ≤ p.K * p.σ ^ 4)
  successful p f output P :=
    Measurable output ∧ ∃ xstar, IsMinOn f Set.univ xstar ∧
      Integrable (fun ω => f (output ω) - f xstar) (P : Measure _) ∧
      ∫ ω, f (output ω) - f xstar ∂(P : Measure _) ≤ p.ε
  allowedAlgorithm p A := ∃ η : ℝ, 0 < η ∧ ∃ Ta Tb : ℕ, A = WindowSgd.method η Ta Tb p.x0

end LongTails.Setups.PLHessianLipschitzKurtosis
